why: A FLOOR ON WHAT MUST SURVIVE A REGENERATION, named rather than counted. gen-completion-registry.js --check only proves the committed file matches what the generator currently produces: both sides come from the same code, so a generator that silently stops emitting real ids passes that check happily. That is not hypothetical. While fixing BUG-277 a character-level comment stripper blanked 87 REAL ids (do-48-dockerfile, ra-w1-kernel-lab, sp-w3-functions-pres and 84 more) and EVERY TEST STILL PASSED, because the ids ceased to exist rather than becoming wrong - no assertion about registry contents can see an absence it was never told to expect. It was caught by a before/after id diff that happened to be run by hand. Nancy's words on the gate: a habit, not a gate. This file is the gate.
how_to_use: completion-validation.test.js asserts every id below is present in functions/completion-registry.json. If one disappears, the generator regressed - do NOT delete the canary to make the test pass. Confirm the content still exists and the page still calls ModuleProgress.complete with that id; only then, if the content was genuinely retired, remove the entry with a note.
not_a_count: Deliberately a SET, not a size threshold. A number goes stale the moment content ships and invites someone to lower it; a named id either survives or something broke. The registry legitimately SHRINKS when a placeholder is removed, which is exactly what BUG-277's correct fix did (-8), so a size floor would have been both wrong and in the way.

house_census: COVERS 12 OF 22 HOUSES BY REAL CALL SITE, and the other 10 deliberately have none. Nancy's block found the first version covered only 7, so a regression confined to web or matrix would have passed every canary. Five houses were added from a derived sweep for literal ModuleProgress.complete call sites, which is the strongest provenance available. The remaining 10 - ala, arena, career, eth, forensics, linux, observatory, platform, signal, windows - have NO literal completion call site anywhere in _app. Their ~640 registry entries each are LearningPaths cross-products (arena-SLO1, platform-SLO1: the 735 declared ids expanded across all 22 houses), so naming one as a canary would canonise an artifact and block a future correct narrowing. That is why this is not a 22-of-22 census, and the three SOURCE GUARD entries cover the extraction paths those houses depend on instead.
sources_guarded: One canary per GENERATOR SOURCE, so no extraction path can go dark unnoticed: literal and resolved call sites (most entries), LearningPaths (shield-cia-triad), trackerKeys (ctf_a1), the legacy floor (CLH-001), ENGINE CONFIG FILES (op-crypto-01, cse-l01, gui-ne10-juniper — added after BUG-279, where an entire unguarded source cost 138 shipped ids including every Operator mission), and INLINE engine configs (hexgrad-engine — added after BUG-280, the same blind spot one shape over, 6 more ids). The pattern is the lesson: each time a source went unguarded, a regression in it was silent until someone happened to look.
